summary:
The HEARTS Act of 2024 amends the Public Health Service Act by inserting new §§ 312A–312D (42 U.S.C. 244a–244d) after § 312 to require federal cardiomyopathy education, awareness, risk-assessment, and reporting activities, authorize NIH-related cardiomyopathy research coordination, and create discretionary grant authority for school AED and CPR programs.

New PHSA § 312A requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the CDC Director, not later than 18 months after enactment, to develop public education materials and resources for school administrators, educators, school health professionals, coaches, families, guardians, caregivers, and other appropriate individuals. Required content includes information on signs, symptoms, and risk factors for cardiomyopathy and specified genetic heart rhythm abnormalities; guidelines for AED placement in schools, early childhood education programs, and child care centers; AED and CPR training information; and recommendations for cardiac emergency response plans. Not later than 30 months after enactment, the Secretary must disseminate these materials through State educational agencies, State and local health departments, pediatricians, hospitals, and other health professionals, and must post them on the CDC website. State educational agencies are encouraged, but not required, to create cardiomyopathy webpages.

New PHSA § 312B requires the Secretary, acting through the CDC Director, not later than 18 months after enactment, to submit to Congress and make public, subject to applicable Federal and State privacy laws, a report on existing CDC activities concerning cardiomyopathy prevalence and epidemiology across the lifespan, including natural history and estimates of related emergency department visits and hospitalizations. The Secretary also must develop and publicly make available a cardiomyopathy risk assessment for providers and individuals, including background information, risk and progression worksheets, and screening guidelines, with external stakeholder input from patient advocacy organizations, medical professional societies, and relevant Federal agencies.

New PHSA § 312C authorizes the Secretary, in consultation with the NIH Director, to expand and coordinate NIH research and related activities on cardiomyopathy, including causation, long-term outcomes, and longitudinal or retrospective treatment/outcomes studies, subject to a nonduplication requirement within HHS. Within 18 months, the Secretary must report to Congress on ongoing NIH research, an adult cardiomyopathy research agenda, pediatric research plans, and greatest research needs.

New PHSA § 312D authorizes discretionary grants to local educational agencies, including qualifying public charter schools, in consultation with qualified health care entities, to promote student access to AEDs and CPR in public elementary and secondary schools. Permissible uses include program materials, training, cardiac emergency response plans, purchase of FDA-approved, cleared, or classified AEDs, batteries and maintenance, and replacement of outdated equipment and materials. Section 2(b) provides that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out §§ 312A–312D.
